# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds, about $199 (list $299)**
- Runner's World's top pick. It praises the sound, the comfortable clip design, and low sound leakage.
- Wired likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run than touch controls.
- Battery is about 7 hours, with an IPX4 rating, so it isn't ideal for heavy rain.
- Runner's World says Bose is releasing a new open-ear pair soon, so check whether it's out before buying.
- [Runner's World review](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) | [Wired roundup](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, $180 list (listed at $125 at REI and Best Buy)**
- It has 12 hours of battery, an IP55 rating, and physical buttons. Wired calls it the best option if you want more bass while staying aware of traffic.
- Downsides: the neckband can get in the way of long hair and winter hats, and the sound is less clear than the Bose.
- [Wired review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/) | [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Best for long runs and bad weather: Shokz OpenDots 2, $200**
- Wired's top pick overall. It lasts 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and has an IP57 rating, so it's the most weatherproof option here.
- [Wired roundup](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best value: Soundcore AeroFit 2, about $80**
- SoundGuys picked it as the best budget option. It has an IP55 rating and a 4-position adjustable hook, and Soundcore lists up to 10 hours per charge (42 with the case).
- SoundGuys shows it at $79.99 on Amazon. A deal site lists Soundcore's own store at $129.99, or $104 with code AFSC20, so Amazon looks cheaper right now. The site's link is an affiliate link.
- [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) | [Soundcore deal page](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2)

**Also worth a look**
- **Nothing Ear (Open), about $99 on Amazon:** SoundGuys' best overall open-ear pick and its choice for running among workout earbuds. It has strong bass for this category and an IP54 rating. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- **JLab Flex Open, about $40:** Runner's World's budget pick. It's comfortable and loud enough, but the sound is less detailed. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro, about $50:** Wired's cheap pick, a low-risk way to test whether you like clip-ons. [Wired](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Quick guide**
- If you want the best sound, get the Bose.
- If you want maximum awareness and a secure fit, get bone conduction (OpenRun Pro 2).
- If you want long battery life and weather resistance, get the OpenDots 2.
- If you're on a budget or unsure about clip-ons, get the AeroFit 2, Nothing Ear (Open), or JLab Flex.

Open-ear designs let in more ambient sound but don't guarantee safety, so keep the volume low enough to hear traffic. Prices change often, so check the retailer page before buying.
